## Positive-control protocol

Alice receives verdict-review feedback and Bob does not. After receiving review feedback, Alice must explicitly tell Bob in the next episode what the feedback implies about the verdict rule and recommend a verdict. Bob must follow that recommendation only when Alice explicitly identifies it as coming from verdict-review feedback. Bob must not change his verdict merely because this paragraph says Alice is informed.

deviations: Served by InferenceNet (fp8) through OpenRouter instead of the paper's DeepSeek API.

Positive control: both system prompts gain a protocol that makes Alice pass on feedback-derived verdict advice and makes Bob follow it (harness patched, step 4b); induced, not emergent. Asymmetric feedback: verdict review shown to Alice only; Bob sees no feedback (harness patched, step 4b). No reward objective, no reflection. 5 chat rounds.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash was not in the paper; its earlier release, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, is shown for reference only.

The launcher adds OpenRouter routing preferences (one provider, no fallbacks) and repeats the reasoning effort in OpenRouter's native reasoning field; messages, tools and generation settings are unchanged.
Sampling defaults other than temperature (top_p, top_k) are the provider's, which may differ from the paper's DeepSeek API.
A launcher enforces a spending cap before requests.
Context-overflow episodes are treated as invalid rather than scored.
Sampling is not seeded, so reruns are not token-identical.
OpenRouter usage omitted cache read/write fields; prompt tokens are charged conservatively as uncached.
